title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government’s response to the Committee’s 2020 report outlines its commitment to strengthening public standards for AI, aiming to improve transparency, fairness, and safety in AI systems. It proposes new regulatory frameworks, investment in research and development, and collaboration with industry and academia to ensure AI technologies benefit society while mitigating risks.

title: EM on EU Regulation 2024/1689 on Artificial Intelligence
description: The government's summary of an EU regulation laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence and amending several Regulations and Directives.
summary: The document explains the EU Regulation 2024/1689, which establishes consistent rules for the development, use, and deployment of artificial intelligence across the European Union. It also describes how this regulation updates and amends existing laws and directives to better manage AI risks and ensure compliance for businesses and public bodies.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual outlines its plan to oversee how AI tools are used in exams and qualifications. The aim is to protect fairness and integrity while allowing technology to support learning and assessment.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report examines how copyright-protected materials are used in building AI models, assessing both the legal and ethical implications. It evaluates the potential risks and benefits, offering guidance on ensuring compliance and protecting creators while fostering AI innovation.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The government responded to the House of Lords Select Committee’s report on AI, outlining its plans to strengthen regulation, ensure safety, and support innovation in the sector. It reaffirmed its commitment to keep the UK as a global leader in AI while addressing concerns about privacy, accountability, and workforce impacts.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: This document outlines the terms of reference for a committee tasked with reviewing how AI affects public standards, including guiding principles and objectives. It also provides frequently asked questions to clarify the committee's scope, responsibilities, and processes.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee regarding the governance of artificial intelligence. In their submission, they outline their perspectives and recommendations on how AI should be regulated and overseen.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: The policy examines how artificial intelligence will change the rules for medical products and the way they are evaluated. It outlines steps to apply the AI White Paper guidelines to keep those products safe, effective, and compliant.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy aims to make the organisation the leading AI-driven defence force for its size, prioritising effectiveness, efficiency, trust and influence. It outlines how AI will be integrated across operations to enhance capability, decision‑making and global standing.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: The report examines how copyrighted works are used in training and developing AI systems under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act, assessing legal compliance and industry practices. It outlines the current status of data usage, identifies key challenges and opportunities, and recommends measures to balance innovation with the protection of copyright holders.
